claim: The comment asserts the default upper-cases unrecognised function names including quoted ones, and PostgreSQL resolves quoted names case-sensitively
source_excerpt:
# normalize_functions=False: the default upper-cases unrecognised function
    # names, quotes included, and PostgreSQL resolves quoted names
    # case-sensitively, so "quote_ident"(x) would become a missing function.
verify_against: sqlglot generator default normalize_functions ('upper') and Anonymous handling
verify_hint: Falsify with apply_rls on base revision for 'SELECT "quote_ident"(name) FROM orders' and check whether output is "QUOTE_IDENT"; check generator.py normalize_func
evidence: Traced sqlglot in .venv (could not execute code; no shell). parser.py:7633-7636: a quoted function name becomes exp.Identifier(quoted=True) inside exp.Anonymous. generator.py:4204-4211 anonymous_sql calls self.func(self.sql(this), ..., normalize=True) for non-qualified names; func() (4941) calls normalize_func (1126-1131), which does name.upper() on the whole string, quotes included, under the default 'upper'. So "quote_ident"(x) is emitted as "QUOTE_IDENT"(x). PostgreSQL treats quoted identifiers as case-sensitive, so that would be a missing function. rls.py:332-335 passes normalize_functions=False, which makes normalize_func return the name unchanged. Hostile input considered: "MyFn"(y) and the qualified a.b.foo() case (anonymous_sql skips normalisation for qualified names; the comment concerns unqualified names, so it still holds). The comment is accurate.

claim: Disabling normalize_functions does not change how recognised built-ins (e.g. COUNT, strpos->POSITION) are printed, nor other rls.py callers that rely on the rewritten SQL text (verify_base_tables routine lookup, readonly guard)
verify_against: sqlglot generator function_fallback_sql / normalize_func; src/sqllens/safety/relations.py routine name extraction
verify_hint: Check existing tests in tests/unit/test_safety_rls.py expecting COUNT(*) uppercase and test_postgres_typed_builtin_with_renamed_canonical_form_is_allowed in tests/unit/test_rls_views.py
evidence: rls.py:335 now calls tree.sql(dialect=dialect, normalize_functions=False). In the installed sqlglot generator.py, normalize_func (l.1126-1131) is the only consumer of the flag and only upper-/lower-cases a name; function_fallback_sql (l.4915-4927) names recognised built-ins via function_name -> expression.sql_name(), which is already canonical upper case (COUNT). ORIGINAL_NAME_META_KEY (generator.py:4930) is set only for drill/bigquery/clickhouse, not postgres/mysql/sqlite, so no written-case leak for built-ins. Dialect-specific transforms (strpos->POSITION/STRPOS) emit literal names and are not affected. Other callers: relations.py:84-107 _called_names tokenises the rewritten SQL and adds text, text.lower() and ASCII-lower, so matching is case-insensitive and unaffected by function-name case; readonly.py:489-498 lower-cases Anonymous names and sql_names(), so the denylist is case-insensitive. The PR's diff also adds tests (test_rls_views.py quoted routine refused, quoted pg_sleep blocked) consistent with this. Only unrecognised (Anonymous) names change, as intended; not run.

claim: RlsGuardRunner refuses quoted "pg_sleep"(1) with UnsafeSqlError, i.e. the denylist check matches quoted function names case-insensitively after the rewrite
verify_against: RlsGuardRunner and dangerous-function denylist in src/sqllens/safety/
verify_hint: Check the function denylist comparison in rls.py / relations.py / readonly.py used by RlsGuardRunner
evidence: RlsGuardRunner.run_sql (src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py:167-197) rewrites via apply_rls, then calls _refuse_denied_functions(rewritten) when rules exist, which calls assert_no_denied_functions (readonly.py:590-604). That parses the rewritten SQL and, for each exp.Func, _func_name_candidates (readonly.py:489-490) returns node.name.lower() for exp.Anonymous; pg_sleep is not a typed sqlglot function, so a quoted "pg_sleep"(1) is Anonymous and its lowercased name matches the lowercase-only denylist (readonly.py:379, enforced lowercase at 461-462). Quotes are not part of node.name. The PR's rewrite change (rls.py:332-335, normalize_functions=False) keeps the written case and quoting, so the rewritten SQL still contains "pg_sleep"(1) and is refused. The test at tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:765 adds this case, expecting UnsafeSqlError matching 'refused by the read-only guard', which is the message from readonly.py:584-587 wrapped by _refuse_denied_functions. Verified by reading only; tests not run.

claim: The connector test's run_sql result is a pandas DataFrame (iloc usable) and quote_ident('alpha') returns 'alpha' unquoted on PostgreSQL
verify_against: build_sql_runner run_sql return type in src/sqllens/agent/factory.py; PostgreSQL quote_ident semantics

evidence: The test (tests/connectors/test_connectors.py:143-153) wraps build_sql_runner(postgres_url) in RowCapRunner, ReadOnlyGuardRunner and RlsGuardRunner, then calls result.iloc[:, 0].tolist(). Every layer declares and returns pd.DataFrame: postgres/sql_runner.py:107-109 (the docstring says DataFrame), limits.py:84-102 (RowCapRunner returns df after df.iloc/copy), safety/__init__.py:92-119 (ReadOnlyGuardRunner) and :163-201 (RlsGuardRunner) both return self._inner.run_sql(...).
